source.anchor_kjv: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
source.thread: Two wounds named in one breath - a bruised heel and a crushed head - and only one of them is fatal
source.hook_line: You've heard Genesis 3:15 means Jesus beats the devil.
source.spoken_script: You've heard Genesis 3:15 means Jesus beats the devil. It says something sharper - one of them gets a bruise, and the other gets a crushed skull. This isn't a tie. God tells the serpent his head will be crushed, and tells the woman's seed only His heel will be bruised - the outcome was fixed before the fight began. God says to the serpent, 'I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.' You might expect matching wounds for a promise this old - instead you get a crushed skull on one side and a survivable bruise on the other. You keep trying to land your own blow against what haunts you, hoping for a tie you can live with. Christ already delivered the blow that ends it. Not a tie - a bruised heel that carried a cross, and a crushed head that stays crushed forever.

platforms.title: Genesis 3:15 Is Not a Tie. Look at the Two Wounds
platforms.description:
You have heard that Genesis 3:15 means Jesus beats the devil. Look closer. One side gets a bruise. The other gets a crushed skull.

"And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel." (Genesis 3:15, KJV)

This is not a tie. A bruised heel is survivable. A crushed head is not. The outcome was fixed before the fight began.

You keep hoping for a tie you can live with. Christ already delivered the blow that ends it: a bruised heel that carried a cross, and a crushed head that stays crushed.
